test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) introduces a specific timeframe for pronouncing judgment after the conclusion of arguments in a criminal trial. What is this timeframe?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Within 30 days (extendable to 45 days)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, which seeks to replace the Indian Penal Code (IPC), introduces significant procedural changes to streamline criminal justice delivery.
 
• One of the provisions under BNSS mandates that judgments in criminal trials must be pronounced **within 30 days** of the conclusion of arguments.
 
• This 30-day period can be extended to a maximum of **45 days** if the court provides valid reasons for the delay.
 
• The provision aims to ensure the **timely delivery of justice** and reduce delays in the judicial process, which have been a longstanding issue in the Indian legal system.
 
• This reform is part of broader efforts to modernize criminal laws and make them more efficient, transparent, and citizen-friendly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Within 7 days**
 
 
• A judgment timeframe of 7 days is not feasible in complex criminal trials, given the need for detailed deliberation, review of evidence, and legal analysis.
 
• Such a short timeframe is not prescribed under any Indian legal code for delivering judgments in criminal cases.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Within 15 days**
 
 
• While shorter timeframes for judgments are desirable, 15 days may not be sufficient in many cases, particularly those involving multiple witnesses, voluminous evidence, or complex legal issues.
 
• No such provision exists in the BNSS or other criminal laws in India.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Within 60 days**
 
 
• A timeframe of 60 days might lead to unnecessary delays in delivering judgments, which the BNSS seeks to minimize.
 
• The BNSS specifically aims to balance timely justice delivery with thorough deliberation, which is why the period is capped at 30 days (extendable to 45 days).
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**
 
 
• The BNSS is part of the proposed reforms to replace existing colonial-era laws such as the Indian Penal Code (IPC), the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), and the Indian Evidence Act.
 
• It emphasizes **citizen-centric reforms**, including provisions to curb delays, enhance accountability, and improve the efficiency of the criminal justice system.
 
• Key features include provisions for faster FIR registration, the use of technology in investigations, and stricter timelines for various stages of trials.
 
• These reforms aim to make India's legal system more **efficient, transparent, and aligned with modern needs**.
